cases.purpose: A nohup child announces readiness with inherited SIGHUP ignored, survives the real terminal hangup, observes EIO on that same terminal, and returns 3 to its waiting parent, which records completion.
cases.oracle: parity vs GNU coreutils 9.7 nohup run by the reference shell; POSIX nohup: SIGHUP ignored in the utility, inherited across exec
cases.comparison: Exact post-hangup observation and exit-status files against GNU nohup; readiness removes the timing assumption that a short sleep must still be active at hangup.

files.observe-hangup.py:
import errno,fcntl,os,signal,sys,termios,time
assert signal.getsignal(signal.SIGHUP)==signal.SIG_IGN
fd=os.open("/dev/tty",os.O_RDWR|os.O_NOCTTY)
os.write(fd,b"NOHUP-READY\n")
deadline=time.monotonic()+5
while time.monotonic()<deadline:
 try: fcntl.ioctl(fd,termios.TIOCGWINSZ,b"\x00"*8)
 except OSError as e:
  if e.errno!=errno.EIO: raise
  open("observed-hangup","w").write("EIO-after-hangup\n");os.close(fd);sys.exit(3)
 time.sleep(0.01)
raise RuntimeError("terminal did not hang up")

cases.script:
nohup /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import errno,os
try:
 data=os.read(0,1); result="EOF" if data==b"" else "DATA"
except OSError as e:
 result=errno.errorcode[e.errno]
print("stdin="+result,flush=True)
os.write(2,b"err")'
